2c49ff36230323cfe2808627cb240ae993693ae3.content:
# Palazzo

Self-hosted internet radio station controller — REST API to push songs, jingles, and live audio into a Liquidsoap/Icecast stream.

Single Docker container: NestJS + Liquidsoap + Icecast2.

## Quick Start

```bash
cp .env.example .env
docker network create broadcast-control 2>/dev/null || true
docker compose up -d
```

API: `http://localhost:3100` — Stream: `http://localhost:8000/stream`

## API

Automation clients should use the private program-scoped surface in
[Program-scoped playout](docs/program-playout.md). It provides atomic
song-plus-intro playout, program-scoped instant/mixer/state/event routes,
durable idempotency, and explicit intro lifecycle reporting.

Push a song: `POST /song` with `{"url": "https://...mp3"}`

All endpoints at a glance:

| Method | Path                                       | Description                                               |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET`  | `/status`                                  | Stream health and metadata                                |
| `GET`  | `/playback/state`                          | Authoritative current playback snapshot                   |
| `GET`  | `/playback/events`                         | Replay-safe Server-Sent Events                            |
| `GET`  | `/metrics`                                 | Private Prometheus telemetry                              |
| `GET`  | `/v1/programs/:programId/automation`       | Private automation lifecycle state                        |
| `POST` | `/v1/programs/:programId/automation/start` | Start the program automation without restarting transport |
| `POST` | `/v1/programs/:programId/automation/stop`  | Clear program material while preserving the Icecast mount |
| `PUT`  | `/v1/programs/:programId/fillers/:version` | Prepare immutable local radio filler from private Alcantara input |
| `GET`  | `/v1/programs/:programId/fillers/:version` | Read filler readiness without exposing signed source data |
| `POST` | `/song`                                    | Push a song, skips current                                |
| `POST` | `/song/stop`                               | Skip current song                                         |
| `POST` | `/instant`                                 | Push a jingle/SFX                                         |
| `POST` | `/instant/stop`                            | Stop all instants                                         |
| `GET`  | `/v1/programs/:programId/output/audio` | Return the configured Icecast audio on the private API |
| `GET`  | `/mixer`                                   | Read the applied song, instant, and main mixer state      |
| `PUT`  | `/mixer`                                   | Apply song, instant, and main volume/mute controls        |
| `GET`  | `/proxy-audio?url=`                        | CORS proxy for audio URLs                                 |

`POST /song` and `POST /instant` accept an optional caller-supplied
`playbackRequestId`, generating one when omitted. Song metadata and that ID
travel with the Liquidsoap request and reappear in lifecycle,
position, and state telemetry. Level samples are emitted at no more than 10 Hz,
position at 1 Hz, and heartbeats approximately every 10 seconds.

The control API, SSE feed, metrics, and Liquidsoap command socket are private
interfaces. The provided Compose and deployment mappings bind
the API to host loopback and join the private `broadcast-control` network;
publish only Icecast (or route it through a reverse proxy) for listeners.
On Cumulus, nginx exposes the same stream at `palazzo.gaulatti.com` and the
Modo Italiano listener hostname `radio.modoitaliano.fm`; the latter redirects
its root to `/stream` and includes the public CORS header used by radio clients.

Container application logs use Docker's host-local `local` driver, bounded to
three 10 MB files per container. Operators can inspect them with
`docker logs --tail 200 palazzo`; Palazzo does not send application logs to
CloudWatch.

For a failed Cumulus deployment, the GitHub Actions job shows SSM remote stdout
and stderr as separate lines and annotates the remote exit code. A missing
deployment token is reported by name without showing its value.

Palazzo boots in `reconciliation-required`: container or process startup never
pretends a prior operator Start/Stop succeeded. Alcantara reconciles it through
the private lifecycle API. Start becomes ready only when Liquidsoap, its
control/telemetry connection, and the Icecast source output are healthy. Stop
flushes both queues and waits for authoritative idle while leaving Liquidsoap
and the 24x7 Icecast mount connected. See
[docs/broadcast-lifecycle.md](docs/broadcast-lifecycle.md).

Full details: [API Reference](wiki/API-Reference)

Telemetry operations and migration guidance:
[docs/playback-telemetry.md](docs/playback-telemetry.md).

## Pull request verification

Local agent review is installed and updated from public Clouseau through the
bastille startup bootstrap. It uses the developer's authenticated Codex or
Claude account and `.clouseau-local.json`; it requires no CI provider keys.
After committing the complete change, run the shared `clouseau` skill, repair
blocking findings, and publish its passing signed receipt before opening a ready
PR. See [local review](https://github.com/gaulatti/clouseau/blob/main/docs/local-review.md).

Every PR runs unit tests with exact 100% line and branch coverage over all
application sources, type-checking, the production dependency audit, workflow
security tests, and real Liquidsoap/Icecast container checks. Run
`npm run test:coverage` locally with Node 22.22.0 and ffmpeg/ffprobe installed.
Native c8 reports include unloaded bootstrap/module files; Clouseau independently
checks the complete source inventory and exact counters.

After those checks pass, a PR carrying an authenticated local review stamp uses
the pinned verifier without AI credentials or an AI rerun. The verifier checks
the enrolled GitHub author, signature, exact source/base, engine and policy,
expiry, literal evidence and calculated scores. Invalid stamps hold approval
without invoking a paid reviewer. Only a protected owner change can enroll or
revoke a workstation key. The enrolled workstation and its privileged processes
are trusted; this is not hardware attestation.

PRs without a stamp retain the separately installed CI reviewer. It assesses purpose, need,
proportionality, technical findings and test integrity. Jev grades its qualified
narrow factors; independent DeepSeek reviews handle the remaining questions.
Passing reviews receive a bot approval and native auto-merge under main's branch
protection. Unresolved product-direction decisions go to gaulatti. Intent
confirmation never waives tests, coverage or integrity. See
[the purpose contract](.github/clouseau.md) and
[Continuous Verification](https://github.com/gaulatti/palazzo/wiki/Continuous-Verification).

Verification and AI review run separately: metadata reassessment does not rebuild
the container, and provider calls wait for real verification to finish. A bot
merge explicitly dispatches the existing deployment workflow for runtime changes;
deployment completion and live stream health remain separate checks.

Protected reviewer installation runs only from the owner-pushed
`policy-install/pr-N` branch at the exact ready PR head, after its matching
`/approve-intent` confirmation. It reuses the PR's independent technical checks
and performs fresh AI assessment before the native approval gate. Manual
dispatch is for verification or reassessment: GitHub excludes dispatched job
checks from required PR checks, so it cannot install the reviewer.

## Documentation

- [Architecture](wiki/Architecture) — System design, data flow, Liquidsoap engine
- [API Reference](wiki/API-Reference) — All endpoints with request/response schemas
- [Configuration](wiki/Configuration) — Environment variables and settings
- [Deployment](wiki/Deployment) — Docker, Compose, CI/CD
- [Development](wiki/Development) — Local setup and project structure

MIT

## Program audio return

Alcántara monitors the encoded output through
`GET /v1/programs/:programId/output/audio`. Palazzo connects only to its own
configured `ICECAST_PORT`/`ICECAST_MOUNT` on loopback, preserving content type
and forwarding bytes incrementally. This private program-scoped endpoint needs
no public listener hostname. Closing the client closes the Icecast connection
without changing broadcast playback. See the wiki API Reference for errors and
monitor metrics.

Production dependency verification uses `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high`.
The Fastify override pins 5.12.5 while keeping NestJS on version 11; remove or
update it only after the adapter resolves a patched version and the HTTP/runtime
gates pass. The unused Dockerode SDK is removed: Palazzo manages its Liquidsoap
child process directly. These dependency corrections preserve metric contracts.

# Palazzo review contract

Palazzo is a single-program internet-radio playout appliance: one container
combines a private NestJS/Fastify control API, Liquidsoap and Icecast. Alcantara
uses it to prepare immutable filler, play songs with optional recorded intros,
mix instants and live audio, observe authoritative playback, and maintain a
continuous listener stream.

Preserve program isolation, private control/telemetry interfaces, durable
idempotency before audible effects, bounded dependency retries and metric labels,
explicit Start/Stop reconciliation, actual media validation, and an uninterrupted
Icecast mount. Command acceptance is not proof of playback; engine observations
and real output bytes establish that result. Startup never invents a prior
operator Start or Stop.

Assess purpose and evidence rather than the number of changed files or lines.
Bug fixes, meaningful tests that raise coverage, dependency repairs, and
operational maintenance can serve this existing appliance without a new product
decision. Browser access to existing private controls, protocol correctness,
recovery, media validation and accurate telemetry are established obligations.
New capabilities must have repository documentation or linked acceptance criteria
that establish their actual need and boundaries.

Ask gaulatti for a second opinion for a product-direction or authority decision:
for example turning the appliance into a content-generation platform, a general
CMS, a multi-tenant hosting service, or a publicly exposed control system.
Ordinary implementation uncertainty and repairable bugs belong to automated
investigation, not routine human code review. Changes to review controls,
coverage exclusions, or this purpose contract require explicit owner confirmation.

Every material capability and mechanism must independently score at least 80 for
fit, need and proportionality under Clouseau's shared protocol. A causal technical
finding at or above 70 blocks; unrelated features or good scores cannot average
away a defect. Integrity and review-completeness gates remain independent.

Tests must assert actual production behavior and failure outcomes. Reject
fabricated coverage, disabled tests, swallowed errors, unconditional assertions,
test-only readiness paths and mocks that replace the behavior being claimed.
External socket, subprocess and filesystem fault injection is legitimate when
the real application contract and failure handling remain exercised. The pinned
container must separately prove real ffmpeg preparation, Liquidsoap control,
Icecast output bytes, lifecycle reconciliation and parsed bounded metrics.

All tests and exactly 100% application line and branch coverage remain mandatory
for every contribution, including external forks. Unloaded bootstrap and module
files must be measured. Missing or unresolved integrity evidence holds approval;
intent confirmation cannot waive it. Contributor code never receives provider,
repair or approval credentials, and fork PRs cannot trigger automatic repairs.

Clouseau owns the shared scoring, investigation, repair bounds, evidence ledger,
native approval and auto-merge. This repository owns its purpose, real tests and
runtime evidence. CI/merge, deployment completion and live health are separate
milestones; a successful merge alone is not a deployment or playback claim.

A passing local Clouseau review may be reused only through a signed receipt from
an enrolled trusted workstation and the matching native GitHub author. CI must
independently verify current protected policy, exact head/base and engine content,
expiry, evidence and deterministic scores. This route has no AI credentials and
must not fall back to paid review when verification fails. All native tests,
exact coverage, container checks and branch protections remain mandatory.
Agent installation and account-authenticated local execution remain independent
of CI enrollment and CI provider keys. A signature authenticates the workstation;
it does not attest against compromise of that workstation or its operator.

local-request.content:
Repair UTF-8 decoding in Palazzo's existing Liquidsoap Telnet client.

Problem: TCP may split a multibyte UTF-8 character between data events. Decoding
each Buffer independently corrupts non-ASCII artist/title metadata. A response
containing Björk, Jóga, Japanese text or emoji must reach the existing response
consumer unchanged regardless of that byte boundary.

Acceptance criteria:
- Decode a single connection's response incrementally before existing END line
  framing, preserving both LF and CRLF response framing and persistent commands.
- Closing, replacing or failing a connection discards its pending decoder bytes
  and response buffer. Partial characters from an old connection cannot contaminate
  a command on the replacement.
- Preserve the existing command queue, timeout/retry limits, stale-socket guards,
  private interface and transport/reconnect metric semantics. No new product
  capability, dependency, public API, deployment mechanism or authority is needed.
- Regression tests exercise real TCP delivery at every byte split for representative
  Unicode metadata and verify replacement-connection isolation. Do not replace the
  production decoder/parser, weaken assertions, exclude sources or relax coverage.
- All established tests and type checks pass with exact 100% line and branch
  application coverage. CI independently retains real radio container verification.
- Update the existing response-framing documentation to describe incremental text
  decoding and connection isolation. The change preserves transport lifecycle and
  metric meanings; it does not introduce a new telemetry dimension.

Keep implementation limited to this concrete protocol-correctness repair and its
regressions/documentation. This requirement is evidence of the requested bugfix,
not permission to change the protected reviewer, signing trust or merge rules.

# Playback telemetry

Palazzo exposes Liquidsoap's observed playback state. It does not infer a
start or end from REST command success, queue length, URL, or estimated
duration.

## Identity and ordering

- `PALAZZO_INSTANCE_ID` is the stable logical instance name. Set it explicitly
  in every deployed environment.
- `bootId` is generated whenever the Palazzo process starts.
- `sequence` increases monotonically. Palazzo reserves a durable billion-value
  range before a boot emits telemetry, so a restarted process begins above the
  previous boot's possible range.
- `playbackRequestId` may be supplied to `POST /song` or `POST /instant`.
  Palazzo generates and returns one when omitted, and attaches it to
  Liquidsoap request metadata in either case.
- An SSE ID is `<bootId>:<sequence>`.

Consumers should fetch `GET /playback/state`, open `GET /playback/events`, and
persist the latest SSE ID. Every connection begins with a versioned `snapshot`
event. Reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`; Palazzo replays missed events when the ID
is still in the 512-event window and otherwise sends the current snapshot. A
changed `bootId` or a sequence gap means the consumer must replace inferred
state with the snapshot before processing new transitions. The sequence cursor
defaults to `/var/lib/palazzo/fillers/playback-event-sequence.json`; startup
fails closed when the durable cursor cannot be read or reserved.

Authoritative program events are `playout.queued`, `preflight.ready`,
`preflight.failed`, `playout.started`, `playout.transitioned`,
`playout.stopped`, `playout.skipped`, and `playout.fallback`. Start, stop, skip,
and transition timestamps come from Liquidsoap lifecycle evidence. Command
acceptance alone never fabricates an audible start.

## Cadence and bounded state

Liquidsoap keeps its most recent 128 lifecycle events. Palazzo keeps its most
recent 512 outward events. Song, instant, and combined-output RMS/peak are
sampled through 100 ms engine windows and published at no more than 10 Hz.
`TELEMETRY_LEVEL_HZ` can lower the rate to 1–10 Hz. Position/status publishes at 1 Hz
and heartbeat at approximately 10 seconds. Track metadata is never used as a
Prometheus label.

## Failure semantics

A Telnet disconnect sets `liquidsoap.connected` to `false` and records
`staleSince`. Palazzo retains the last-known track and measurements because a
transport failure is not evidence that audio ended. Palazzo restarts a failed
Liquidsoap child with capped exponential backoff. After reconnect, a fresh
snapshot and the engine journal reconcile lifecycle state. A lower engine
sequence is treated as a restart without fabricating a track-end event.

Each Telnet connection owns its response buffer and transport callbacks. After
a timeout creates a replacement, delayed data, close, error or write callbacks
from the old socket cannot complete or reject the replacement's command. A
successful recovery still counts one Telnet reconnect attempt; ignored stale
callbacks do not trigger another reconnect or change the retry limits.

Useful metrics:

- `palazzo_build_info{service="palazzo",version="..."}`
- `palazzo_process_*` and `palazzo_nodejs_*` runtime/process families
- `palazzo_telemetry_connected`
- `palazzo_telemetry_sample_age_seconds`
- `palazzo_telemetry_poll_failures_total`
- `palazzo_telnet_reconnects_total`
- `palazzo_liquidsoap_restarts_total`
- `palazzo_track_lifecycle_total{event="started|ended"}`
- `palazzo_media_preflight_total{result,reason}`
- `palazzo_playout_transitions_total{event}`
- `palazzo_sse_subscribers`
- `palazzo_sse_event_buffer_events` and replay-drop counters
- normalized-route HTTP request and duration counters
- `palazzo_dependency_operations_total{dependency="liquidsoap",operation,result}`
- `palazzo_dependency_retries_total{dependency="liquidsoap",operation}`

Alert on a disconnected bridge or growing sample age. Do not alert on a
last-known active track alone while the bridge is stale.

The dependency labels are closed enums. They distinguish successful telemetry
polls, transport failures, parse failures, unexpected process exits, Telnet
connection retries, and child-process restart attempts without carrying error
messages. Palazzo currently spawns Liquidsoap directly and makes no Docker API
calls, so it deliberately exposes no fabricated Docker dependency metric.

## Security boundary

Liquidsoap Telnet has no authentication and binds only to `127.0.0.1` inside
the container. The API and SSE mappings bind to host loopback in Compose and
deployment. `GET /metrics` is available only on that private interface. The
central `gaulatti/prometheus` deployment must join `broadcast-control` and
scrape `http://palazzo:3100/metrics`; central scrape,
dashboard, and alert configuration remain outside this repository.

Metric labels are limited to normalized HTTP method/route/status, fixed
playback event/replay types, fixed dependency operation/result values,
prom-client runtime buckets/kinds/version components, and bounded service/build
identity. Program IDs, instance IDs, playback request IDs, media metadata,
URLs, credentials, and free-form errors never appear in exposition. SSE event
payloads and snapshot events also remove URL-, token-, password-, credential-,
and credential-shaped fields. The private REST state remains the
authoritative debugging surface for current engine metadata.
The prom-client active-handle, active-request, and active-resource type
families are excluded because library-defined async-resource names do not
satisfy that closed-label contract; the remaining Node/process baseline is
retained.

## Runtime compatibility

The container pins the official Liquidsoap 2.4.5 multi-architecture image and
Node 22.22.0 image by immutable digest. Before changing either digest:

1. Run `npm test` and `npm run typecheck`.
2. Generate the script and validate it with the target Liquidsoap
   `liquidsoap --check` command.
3. Build the image for both `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`.
4. Play a known finite track and verify request ID, metadata, start, position,
   non-zero levels, end, idle state, SSE replay, and a private metrics
   scrape that parses as Prometheus text.
5. Interrupt the command connection while a track plays and verify Palazzo
   marks telemetry stale without emitting a false `track.ended` event.

Existing callers remain compatible: the original control routes and `ok`
field are unchanged. Callers may ignore the added `playbackRequestId` and the
new `playback` member on `GET /status` until they adopt telemetry.

Problem: TCP may split a multibyte UTF-8 character between data events. Decoding

## Failure semantics

A Telnet disconnect sets `liquidsoap.connected` to `false` and records
`staleSince`. Palazzo retains the last-known track and measurements because a
transport failure is not evidence that audio ended. Palazzo restarts a failed
Liquidsoap child with capped exponential backoff. After reconnect, a fresh
snapshot and the engine journal reconcile lifecycle state. A lower engine
sequence is treated as a restart without fabricating a track-end event.

Each Telnet connection owns its response buffer and transport callbacks. After
a timeout creates a replacement, delayed data, close, error or write callbacks
from the old socket cannot complete or reject the replacement's command. A
successful recovery still counts one Telnet reconnect attempt; ignored stale
callbacks do not trigger another reconnect or change the retry limits.

Telnet response text is decoded incrementally as UTF-8 before line framing, so
artist names and other metadata survive a character split across TCP chunks.
Closing or replacing a connection discards its partial character along with its
response buffer; bytes from different connections are never combined.

| `POST` | `/instant`                                 | Push a jingle/SFX                                         |
| `POST` | `/instant/stop`                            | Stop all instants                                         |
| `GET`  | `/v1/programs/:programId/output/audio` | Return the configured Icecast audio on the private API |
| `GET`  | `/mixer`                                   | Read the applied song, instant, and main mixer state      |
| `PUT`  | `/mixer`                                   | Apply song, instant, and main volume/mute controls        |
| `GET`  | `/proxy-audio?url=`                        | CORS proxy for audio URLs                                 |

`POST /song` and `POST /instant` accept an optional caller-supplied
`playbackRequestId`, generating one when omitted. Song metadata and that ID
travel with the Liquidsoap request and reappear in lifecycle,
position, and state telemetry. Level samples are emitted at no more than 10 Hz,
position at 1 Hz, and heartbeats approximately every 10 seconds.

The control API, SSE feed, metrics, and Liquidsoap command socket are private
interfaces. The provided Compose and deployment mappings bind
the API to host loopback and join the private `broadcast-control` network;
publish only Icecast (or route it through a reverse proxy) for listeners.
On Cumulus, nginx exposes the same stream at `palazzo.gaulatti.com` and the
Modo Italiano listener hostname `radio.modoitaliano.fm`; the latter redirects
its root to `/stream` and includes the public CORS header used by radio clients.

Container application logs use Docker's host-local `local` driver, bounded to
three 10 MB files per container. Operators can inspect them with
`docker logs --tail 200 palazzo`; Palazzo does not send application logs to
CloudWatch.

For a failed Cumulus deployment, the GitHub Actions job shows SSM remote stdout
and stderr as separate lines and annotates the remote exit code. A missing
deployment token is reported by name without showing its value.

Palazzo boots in `reconciliation-required`: container or process startup never
pretends a prior operator Start/Stop succeeded. Alcantara reconciles it through
the private lifecycle API. Start becomes ready only when Liquidsoap, its
control/telemetry connection, and the Icecast source output are healthy. Stop
flushes both queues and waits for authoritative idle while leaving Liquidsoap
and the 24x7 Icecast mount connected. See
[docs/broadcast-lifecycle.md](docs/broadcast-lifecycle.md).
